thread:
Maya K: Heads-up — exploring a bastionless private deploy pattern for customers who want no jump host. Question: how should we wire KMS attestation + RBAC so operators can still revoke access quickly without opening egress?
Ben I: +1 on bastionless. My quick idea: device attestation -> keystamp (signed blob from local HSM/HW TPM) -> short SVID-like lease from our KMS proxy. Revoke by blacklisting stamp at control plane.
Maya K: Can you sketch the keystamp flow? curious about offline/airgapped fallback.
Ben I: Flow (super rough):
```
1) node boots, TPM generates keypair
2) keystore agent asks local HSM for stamp: sign(nonce||node-id||pubkey)
3) agent writes stamp to /var/lib/redwood/keystamp
4) when caller requests token, agent presents stamp to local KMS-shim; shim verifies stamp and mints short token
```
If no upstream, shim can mint a sealed fallback token tied to stamp, short TTL. Ops revoke = push blacklist to agents when they reconnect.
Raj P: For airgapped customers we should avoid any mandatory outbound ACLs. Suggest storing audit-forward buffer locally (compressed) and ship over customer-approved channels. Also implement a conntrack-aware egress limiter so a compromised process can't open thousands of sockets.
Lila S: Audit question — if we buffer locally, what's the minimal retention we keep before ship? customers often demand 90 days for compliance. We can't guarantee that in offline mode. Need explicit contract language.
Sam O: Vulnerability note: there's a CVE in a transitive dependency of our keystore-agent (libnss-async). If agent runs as root and has CTL_NET privileges, exploit can open egress. Short term mitigation: run agent unprivileged, move conntrack limits to kernel drop on cgroup.
Maya K: Good catch Sam. Can you create a triage thread + PoC detection rule?
Sam O: Will do — quick detection snippet:
```
# psuedo: detect rapid outbound connect attempts per cgroup
iptables -N RATECHK
iptables -A OUTPUT -m recent --name KEEPACT --rcheck --seconds 10 -j DROP
# better: eBPF per-cgroup connect counter -> alert
```
Raj P: Also proposing RBAC tightening: token minted by shim must be audience-limited (only allowed to call keystore decrypt endpoint) and single-purpose. Use short TTL (30s) and require proof-of-possession for any downstream gRPC streams.
Ben I: Agree. For revocation we should accept a stamped revocation list (S-RL) signed by the control plane. Agents will check S-RL at reconnect. For faster local evictions, add a local policy that rejects tokens if keystamp stale > X or agent sees revocation marker file from ops.
Maya K: How do we validate keystamp integrity without contacting control plane? TPM sig verification only, but we need to know the allowed set of attestation keys. Ship a key-allowlist blob in the offline bundle; rotate on reconnect.
Lila S: And audit logs: make sure each keystore decrypt request logs: request_id, caller_stamp_hash, op, result_code, local_seq_id. Store in append-only file with signed checkpoint periodically so user can prove log integrity.
Sam O: Ops/incident playbook: if we suspect compromise, we should: 1) create immediate S-RL entry for affected stamp 2) push advisory to customer (if online) 3) instruct them to run agent sweep that flips local quarantine flag -> agent kills worker processes and drops new tokens.
Maya K: Can we make the quarantine flag require a locally-signed attestation to avoid accidental self-bricking?
Raj P: Yes, require two-party approval: local admin signs flag and operator also signs S-RL; agents accept quarantine only when both present. Prevents accidental mass-quarantine.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: staging/keystore-agent v1.8.3 -> canary start 6155556796 ; logs -> /var/log/redwood/keystore-agent.log
Lila S: Action items: Sam -> open vuln triage ticket + detection rule; Raj -> RFC of keystamp format + S-RL proposal; Ben -> prototype conntrack/cgroup limiter + eBPF PoC; Maya -> update incident playbook with quarantine two-party flow and offline audit obligations.
Maya K: Thanks — feel free to ping me for pairing on the RFC. :thumbsup:
